notes.title: Do you dare take on the Witch Ring Challenges? Patch 1.3.0 is here with a new challenge!

items.text: Hey, Pilots! ✈️
Autumn is here, Halloween just happened, and we at Tiny Roar are also totally in a witchy mood! 🎃

With your help, and thanks to your feedback over the last few months (we honestly can't believe it's been that long since release already!), we’ve been busy fixing bugs, addressing your most urgent concerns, and making Lou’s Lagoon overall more enjoyable to play. Now, it’s time to add a little something extra: a brand-new challenge that will put your gliding skills to the test! Want a little hint at what awaits you?
🧹Witches' magic is to fly
high on broomsticks through the sky!
Not a problem, broomstick's ditched!
A Glider's just as much bewitched.
Find three courses, do the "pop!
Come right back once you're on top!🪄

Once you’ve unlocked the glider and properly entered Gleam Reef, keep an eye out for the witch Ryma waiting for you across all islands (though the Boulderians will need a little extra help before he arrives on theirs). 👀

Conquering these trials will reward you with a brand-new witchy outfit! This is the very reward you all unlocked together by hitting our community launch stretch goals. Thank you so much again for all your support! We’ve also been hard at work on the next goal, the dual-toned hair customization, which is also available in this update! Now your characters can look even more stylish and individual!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42720288/d45c6045e2ff8777ce7024ab1f9adc455653ceb1.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42720288/53935b3df9817ded68b3983c38a0750ed0257483.png"]

notes.title: 🎃 No need for FOMO: A Permanent Addition!

items.text: Even though this update brings a fun touch of Halloween flavor, it is a permanent addition to the game! Take your time and don’t feel stressed, you won’t miss out on anything if you don’t get to play right away.
This also means that our Nintendo Switch players will get to enjoy these challenges just the same when the update lands on Switch a little later on, even if Halloween has already passed by then.
Alongside the new challenges, we’ve bundled in several other fixes and quality-of-life tweaks, which you can find in the full notes below.
Find the witch Ryma to take on her challenge and prove that you too possess magic abilities!
The Witch Challenges are 12 all-new ring challenges across all islands that can be done with the Glider of various gadget levels.
Completing the challenges on each island rewards a part of the new Witch Attire.
\[Community Goal] Added secondary hair colors. Visit a stylist to set a secondary hair color for existing characters.

Instead of extending glide time with each gadget level, the Glider now has boosts that can be activated similarly to the plane boosts. Each Glider gadget level adds an additional boost. Boosts only recharge while on the ground.
Greatly reduced the cooldown for opening or closing the Glider.
Opening the Glider now generates much less heat.
The heat gauge now resets after landing, making it possible to immediately switch to swirling or gliding again.
Added the option to increase the text size.
Added control rebinding on consoles.
Added buttons to set the minimum and maximum quantity when choosing item amounts in shops or factories.
Made the Scooper scan highlight more prominent so it is easier to recognize.
Improved quest giver portrait textures to make them look crisper.
“Continue” is now the default selection in the main menu.
Fixed being able to complete the quest “An Old Friend” without ever going to Eastal. This also fixes a related crash on consoles.
Fixed an incorrect collision on the big tree in Tanglebloom Town.
Fixed shops showing unique items the player already owns and therefore can’t buy.
Fixed an issue where a swirl visual effect would appear on the player character while sprinting.
Fixed visible “holes” in the player character when wearing certain clothing combinations.
Fixed drones going to sleep immediately after returning instead of landing properly.
Fixed overlapping duplicate labels on save slots in the Save/Load menu.
Fixed the quest “Bad Omen” showing as unfinished even though it had already been completed.
Fixed a dialogue in which Bartir mentions the Builder gadget before the player has acquired it.
Fixed an issue where the Glider tutorial could overlay Fidge’s dialogue after unlocking the Glider.
Fixed the final encounter with Bartholomew starting too early after loading a save made before the encounter.
Don’t forget to let us know how you like the new update, either here in the Steam discussions or over on our Discord server, where we always love to welcome you for a chat! 🫶

Hey, Pilots! 🛩️
First of all: thank you all so much for your continuous feedback!

Now that Lou’s Lagoon is out, its development really feels like a communal effort. Even with a few initial hiccups at launch, we couldn’t be happier with all the input you've been sending our way, and we’re doing our absolute best to jump on it quickly. Thank you, and keep the feedback coming! 🫶
With it come a ton of bugfixes, as well as some quick improvements to the most pressing feedback.

🐝 Shorter crafting and drone delivery times: Crafting times, as well as the drone delivery times have been reduced. We initially imagined crafting to be something that happens in the background while you go on in your adventures and visit other islands. We see now that that’s simply not the way Lou’s Lagoon is being played, and that shorter crafting times enable you to fulfill your current quests more smoothly. We’re very eager to hear from you whether crafting feels better now!

🛩️Expanded Plane Storage: The plane storage has been upped from 12 to 20 slots, and it can be accessed from anywhere on the islands. We hope that this is an effective quick fix for your storage concerns. At the same time, as pointed out in our previous post, this might be subject to changes in the future when the silos, the “real” alternative, arrive.

🧰Improved guidance towards treasure chests: We improved guidance towards treasure chests on all islands. If you haven’t found all of them yet, maybe now’s the time! This change is less about simply making it “easier” to find the chests, but rather about doing a better job highlighting the special spots where rewards are waiting.
Oh, and we added a small cutscene to flying into the tornado!🌪️ It should now feel less like a placeholder animation, and more ✨dramatic✨ instead.

items.text: Hey Pilots!

We have just launched update 1.0.5 which contains important hotfixes that are listed below. It's also time to share more about our roadmap for the next two weeks. Right now, our focus is on fixing bugs and improving the current experience, so please don't expect any massive new features over the next two weeks. That being said, there will still be some smaller new features coming your way.

Early next week, we aim to deliver our first major patch. This will be Version 1.1.0, which resolves many bugs, blockers, and crashes. One issue that caused a lot of trouble was players getting stuck in the environment. We have an initial fix for this and are confident that it will clear up most of those problems.
The patch also brings changes to the Cargo system. You will now be able to access your cargo from anywhere, and we are adding 8 additional slots.
Why are we doing this, and couldn't we have just expanded the inventory instead?

Currently, cargo can be very frustrating. You run out of space in your Zipper, and the plane is too far away (or in the worst case, behind a loading screen… looking at you, Norleaf). Still, we don't want to abandon inventory management entirely, and we think it's important that players still have the next Zipper upgrade to look forward to. That's why we chose this as the quickest solution to implement. Will it stay like this forever? We don't know yet, but for now, it's a solid compromise.
We're also reducing crafting times so you won't have to wait as long to make materials!

In the following patch, alongside other fixes, we want to release the Silo. This should take even more pressure off the inventory situation. The Silo will be a fixed building that you can upgrade to get even more space. Additionally, crafting stations will be able to pull resources directly from both the Silo and the Cargo. This will eliminate the annoying hassle of moving items back and forth.
On top of that, there will be further improvements to building and the Ring Challenges.
Crashes
Fixed a crash tied to customisation pieces that could occur when landing the seaplane.
Bugfixes
Fixed a blocker that prevented receiving the Wind Cassette if the player flew into the storm prior to having received the Empty Cassette.
Fixed being able to remove the basic Refinery by hitting "Undo" in the Builder menu without having anything else built. Will not affect Save Games where the basic Refinery has already been removed.
Fixed a blocker that made Boulderia's chains invisible.
Achievements
Fixed the trigger for the "Storm Chaser" achievement.
Fixed the trigger for the "What Meets the Eye" achievement.

Thank you so much for all of your feedback and please keep it coming! We hope you'll continue enjoying your time on the Limbo Archipelago as we roll out these improvements along with more changes in the future!
~ The Lou's Lagoon Team

releases.displayName: Project Update: The new and improved Lou's Island! 🏝️🐝

items.text: Hey Pilots! 🛩️

In our last update, we gave you a peek behind the curtain at what we’ve been working on. From smaller tweaks like shorter nights to the big overhauls we made to fishing and exploration. But the biggest changes are definitely due to that "Sandbox Prototype" we tested internally, which sparked some massive changes for Lou’s Island.
Today, we want to share more details on what those changes look like, how your home base is evolving, and introduce a few new machines (and a buzzing new feature) coming to the game because of it!

notes.title: 🏘️ Lou’s Island: It Takes a Village 🏘️

items.text: In our older versions and last year's demo, Lou’s Island served as the central point of the archipelago, but it didn’t quite feel like a true base of operations yet. Sure, Hefti (the absolute best mechanic around) was already there, but then again Clip and Clap were occasionally more of a hindrance than a help!

We wanted your home base to feel alive, so we’ve changed how the island grows. Now, as you explore and find them, Fidge and Bobster will actually move into their very own little houses on Lou’s Island.
Fidge will be your go-to for gadget upgrades.
Bobster finds a home (after he’s done working on the archipelago’s radio towers!)
Jackie also decided to move her boat just a little closer to everyone else, so you’re all together in the little bay 🫶

And of course, Granny and Clip and Clap are still on the island, and everyone worked together to move Granny from her lonely spot on the hill to your little community hub. And with that, there are just a few more targets around for Clip and Clap’s pranks 👀.
It really changes the vibe - you’re no longer alone out there, you’re building a community!
We’ve worked hard to make gathering resources in Lou’s Lagoon satisfying, but it’s still nice to not have to do all the work by yourselves, right?
Enter the drones!

By setting up drone stations, you can get a little help from these bee-eautiful automated assistants. Once you’ve discovered a resource for the first time, these little guys can help gather it over time to make your next big building project a little easier.

During the "Sandbox Prototype" phase, we were just using temporary placeholder assets, but our art team went to town on the final designs. This final bee-inspired version absolutely won our hearts and we hope you like it as much as we do! And look at their cute custom animations for taking off, returning back home, and dropping off what they collected! 🐝🥰

notes.title: 🛠️ New Machines: Processing Resources the Way They Deserve 🛠️

items.text: As we re-balanced the game, we realized that raw driftwood, scrap metal, and raw wool aren't exactly the sturdiest materials to build a civilization with. Processed resources are playing a much bigger role now, which means you're going to need a bigger workshop.
Say hello to The Refiner, The Processor, The Manufacturer, and The Loomer!
You’ll be able to build and place all of these on your island, and each one unlocks a completely new tier of materials:
The Refiner: Used to treat and improve core building materials like wood, metal, and rock.
The Processor: This one’s here to process foods - basically a mill and a juicer combined!
The Manufacturer: For the fine details. Think small mechanical parts like screws or microchips.
The Loomer: Turns that messy raw wool into neat, usable textiles.
Building up this production line makes Lou's Island feel like a functioning, useful home base, and we can't wait to see your layouts.

We’re also working on setting up the Job Board. It’s going to give you a comfortable way to check out all available tasks right from your home on Lou’s Island. After all, repairing those radio towers has to be good for something, and what better use than keeping you updated on the islanders’ needs from afar?

As always, thank you all for the incredible support and for letting us take the time to realize Lou's Lagoon the way that feels right to us. And luckily, you won’t have to wait long until you can inspect some of these changes yourself and visit the new and improved Lou’s Island! 🏝️🤭
Let us know what you think of the new village setup and the drones in the comments, or over on our Discord server!
Best, The Lou’s Lagoon Crew ✈️🌴

releases.displayName: Project Update: The "Sandbox Prototype" and a whole bunch of overhauls! 🛩️

items.text: We know we’ve been a bit quiet lately, and we really appreciate you sticking around! 🥰 As we get closer to our launch later this year, we wanted to pull back the curtain and give you a little more insight into what’s actually been happening behind the scenes of Lou’s Lagoon.

While we’d originally planned to be purely in "bug-fixing and polishing" mode by now 👀, we hit a point where we had to be honest with ourselves and admit that some parts of the game just weren't hitting the vibe we wanted. Based on recent playtests, the balance between letting you explore freely and giving you enough guidance was not where we wanted it to be (and that balance has been a topic of A LOT of internal discussions!) So, we decided to roll up our sleeves and make some bigger changes to get it right:

While most of the team kept improving the main game, a few of us formed a little "task force" to build what we just called “the prototype” or "sandbox prototype". We wanted to experiment with the quest structure and rethink Lou’s Island (the first place you land) and its function in the game. We tried out a central hub, new machines, and... we may have even added pretty cool drones as well! 🙂‍↕️

When the day finally came to play it internally, it was an "all-hands" feedback session. To be honest, we didn't love every single change (but that was to be expected), but the new role of the main island felt amazing. It’s now a place where your favorite characters actually hang out together as a team and their aid in your quest will be very noticeable.
We’re still tweaking the visuals, but we’ll show more details on the changes to Lou’s Island very soon!

We’ve been spending a lot of time flying around our own world, and we noticed that we need to fill the overworld with more incentive for you to explore it. After all, we don’t just want your plane to be a tool for getting from A to B, we want flying to be a fun and integral part of the game! And without a good reason to fly under arches and through tight spaces you might miss the best views! 🪽

To fix that, we’re testing out ways to implement quests in the overworld, so the journey between islands feels like part of the adventure rather than just travel time. 🙂‍↕️ We’ll have more info soon, as this is very much in the making right now.
Oh, and we gave some more drama to the tornado. You’ll definitely think twice before not taking it seriously now! 🌪️
Fishing felt a bit flat in earlier versions and has been a constant object of iteration, and we’ve done a big balancing pass to make fishing more of a fun challenge:
Fish spawns are now time-sensitive (day vs. night) and island-specific. ☀️🌘
Your rod level now matters a little more for the types of fish you’ll hook, and you’ll have more reason to upgrade it! 🎣

We made some small changes to the fishing minigame itself. It’s less about hitting buttons quickly and now focuses on keeping the fish inside a circle. It feels much more satisfying, intuitive, and captures that feeling of having to lean into the pull to land your catch. We can’t wait for when you’ll be able to try it out yourself! 🐟
Finally, we’ve been tackling a huge list of "quality of life" stuff based on your feedback. Honestly, there’s been so many little changes!

The towns now feel livelier, as the NPCs have more animations and move around instead of staying in one spot, and you’ll also find a stylist in every town now! The crab that Boulderia is built on also got more animations, and a little more personality with that. Nights are now shorter (as befits the sunny island setting), we’ve added a controller rumble function, the map has been improved, there’s now a visual indication of your gadgets’ level, and many building objects have interactive functions... Well, a lot has happened!!
Thanks for reading this wall of text, and thank you for being with us. We’re working hard to make Lou’s Lagoon the best version of itself, and we can't wait to share more with you very soon. 🥰
Best, The Lou’s Lagoon Crew ✈️🌴
Hey Pilots! ✈️
We wanted to let you know that we’ll be taking the demo for Lou’s Lagoon offline later today for a while. Why? Because it’s time to put it under construction! 🛠️

You gave us a lot of feedback—what you loved, what needed a bit more polish, and everything in between—and we’ve been listening! Based on your feedback, we’re hard at work improving both Lou’s Lagoon as a whole as well as the demo.
Thank you so much for playing, sharing your thoughts, and being part of this journey with us. We’ll let you know when our demo is back up and better than ever before! 🥰
Stay tuned for updates! ✈️✨
The Tiny Roar Team
A very small update introducing some analytics fixes. This should not otherwise impact the demo.

Made some tweaks to the quest flow

Fixed some placement & wording of button input prompts
